items.title: EU to ban social media for under 13s, curb access until 15
items.summary: STRASBOURG, France: The European Union will ban social media for children under 13 and allow only limited, supervised access until the age of 15 under plans unveiled Wednesday by EU chief Ursula von der Leyen. "It is time for Europe to act," von der Leyen said during her annual keynote address to the European Parliament. "No social media under the age of 13.

items.title: Health minister visits family of FDS nurse killed in heli crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad visited the late nurse Debra Moset at their home in Rabak Rimu, Kampung Semadang, Padawan, today. A social media post on the Health Ministry's Facebook page today showed Dzulkefly spending time with members of Debra's family, including her mother, Renog Rasas, 71, and the late nurse's children. The visit was also attended by Health Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad and Sarawak Health Department deputy director (Management) Banges Munga.

items.title: 19 hikers rescued after four-hour ordeal at Lata Debu
items.summary: BALING: Firefighters rescued 19 people who were trapped following a flash flood at Lata Debu today. District fire and rescue station chief Zulkhairi Mat Tanjil said his team received a distress call at 4.11pm. "They were believed to have been making their way down when they became trapped following the flash flood and strong currents," he said when contacted today.

items.title: Kosovo's ex-president Thaci jailed for 25 years for war crimes
items.summary: PRISTINA: Kosovo's former president Hashim Thaci was sentenced to 25 years by a tribunal in The Hague on Wednesday for war crimes, the court said in a long-awaited verdict likely to spark outrage in the Balkan country. Thaci's fellow former Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) figures Jakup Krasniqi, Rexhep Selimi and Kadri Veseli were also found guilty and sentenced. Krasniqi received 25 years in prison, Selimi got 13 years and Veseli 18 years.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - September 16, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Here are today's top stories. Yeoh explains input Hannah Yeoh says her input on Najib Razak's pardon application was given honestly and in the nation's best interest. Muhyiddin charges remain The Attorney-General says three Jana Wibawa charges against former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin are still being pursued.

items.title: Angkasa president elected to ICA Board, Malaysia retains seat in global cooperative body
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Angkatan Koperasi Kebangsaan Malaysia Bhd (Angkasa) president Datuk Seri Dr Abdul Fattah Abdullah has been elected as an International Cooperative Alliance (ICA) Board member for the 2026-2030 term. In a statement, Angkasa said the victory came through an election held during the ICA General Assembly 2026 in Panama, enabling Malaysia to retain its place in the top leadership of the world cooperative movement's apex body. Angkasa vice president Datuk Kamarudin Ismail's held the same position for the 2022-2026 term.

items.title: Anwar, Abang Johari witness official handover of Bintulu Port to Sarawak
items.summary: KUCHING: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg today witnessed the official handover of Bintulu Port to the Sarawak state government from the federal government, marking a new chapter in the management of the strategic port. "With the coming into force of Act 858 and Act 859 on Sept 1, Bintulu Port officially changed its status from a federal port to a state port under the jurisdiction of the Sarawak government," the statement said. The transition also saw the dissolution of the Bintulu Port Authority (LPB), with the port authority functions taken over by the Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak), a state statutory body established under the Port Authorities Ordinance 1961.

items.title: Nissan to build new hybrid SUV model for Europe at its UK plant
items.summary: LONDON: Japanese automaker Nissan said on Wednesday it would build a new hybrid small SUV for Europe at its UK plant in Sunderland and would invest £170 million (US$229 million) to assemble it there. The company said the Kicks e-POWER hybrid would be made in Sunderland alongside the Qashqai, Juke and electric Leaf models, but it did not provide a timeline for production. There have been concerns over the future of the Sunderland plant, which is Britain's largest car assembly plant.

items.title: Volvo Malaysia rolls out electric EX30 Cross Country
items.summary: VOLVO Car Malaysia has introduced the locally assembled Volvo EX30 Cross Country, an all-electric compact SUV designed for urban driving and light off-road use. Priced from RM218,888, excluding insurance, the model is the first fully electric vehicle in Volvo's Cross Country range. The EX30 Cross Country is powered by a twin-motor all-wheel-drive system producing 428hp and 543Nm of torque.

items.title: McLaren to invest US$675 million to expand UK manufacturing, launch SUV model
items.summary: LONDON: British supercar maker McLaren said on Tuesday it would invest £500 million (US$675 million) in its UK manufacturing and engineering operations and add new models, including its first-ever SUV, to lift sales and pursue far higher profit margins to rival the likes of Ferrari. "McLaren Automotive is doubling down on Britain," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in a statement. McLaren CEO Nick Collins told Reuters the company's investment plan comes after restructuring last year following its acquisition by Abu Dhabi's CYVN Holdings, which also bought a non-controlling stake in McLaren's Formula One business.

items.title: Missing Klang angler found dead in Perak waters
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The body of an angler reported missing since Sunday was found floating in the waters off Hutan Melintang, Perak. North Klang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Ramsay Embol said the search and rescue (SAR) team was alerted to the discovery by a group of fishermen at 8.30am. "The body was taken by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) to Hutan Melintang Jetty.

items.title: Police confirm body found in Perak waters is missing angler
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 16 —Police have confirmed that the body of a man found floating in the waters off Hutan Melintang, Perak, this morning is one of the three anglers missing since Monday. Klang Utara police chief ACP Ramsay Embol said the body was identified as Mohd Sharil Abd Rahman, 43, following identification by next-of-kin. Ramsay said the joint SAR operation to locate the two remaining missing victims is ongoing.

items.title: 'Why didn't you come and see me?' - Dr Akmal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The plight of a family living in poor conditions without water and electricity in Merlimau has caught the attention of assemblyman Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh. Unable to pay an electricity bill amounting to RM2,387.32 and a water bill of RM5,000, the family had resorted to using candles at night, while relying on neighbours for water. In the video, Dr Akmal was seen expressing shock at the condition of the house occupied by the family, which was partially without a roof.

items.title: Diesel, RON97 and unsubsidised RON95 prices up by RM0.35 for Sept 17-23 period
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — The retail prices of RON97 petrol, unsubsidised RON95 petrol and unsubsidised diesel will each increase by 35 sen per litre for the Sept 17-23 period, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said. In a statement today, MOF said the retail price of RON97 would increase to RM4.85 per litre from RM4.50, while unsubsidised RON95 would rise to RM4.37 from RM4.02 and unsubsidised diesel to RM5.27 from RM4.92. The ministry said the increase in global fuel prices was driven by heightened tensions in West Asia amid the conflict, which has entered its 200th day.

items.title: Five Orang Asli held at Tasek Bera released on police bail
items.summary: BERA: The five Orang Asli arrested for allegedly obstructing an enforcement team during a joint operation at the Tasek Bera Conservation Forest Reserve (Ramsar) yesterday have been released on police bail. District police chief Superintendent Zulkiflee Nazir said the five, including four women aged between 30 and 65, were released about 5pm today. The enforcement operation involved the Pahang State Enforcement Unit, Forestry Department, Bera District and Land Office, General Operations Force, Wildlife and National Parks Department and police.

items.title: Pas chief Hadi gives statement over US claim to topple BN govt
items.summary: Pas president's political secretary Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman said Hadi gave the statement in Kuala Lumpur several days ago. "Tan Sri Tuan Guru (Hadi) has given a statement to the police several days ago in Kuala Lumpur. The US Embassy, however, denied Hadi's claim.

items.title: Armed forces proved capabilities in NATO mission, says veteran
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The professionalism and capabilities of the armed forces came to the fore on the world stage when it made history as the first military force from Asia to participate in a North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) mission through the Implementation Force (IFOR), a peace enforcement force, in Bosnia in 1995. Armed forces veteran Major General (Rtd) Datuk Mohamad Raih Ismail said that before being accepted to participate in the more challenging IFOR mission, the Malaysian contingent first underwent rigorous tests by NATO. "The best experience we gained was proving that our forces could work with other foreign military forces at a very professional level," he said.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia agree to cooperate on transboundary haze
items.summary: We will cooperate to reduce the impact of transboundary haze," he told reporters after the official handover of Bintulu Port from the Federal Government to the Sarawak Government at Kuching International Airport here today. [[nid:1534188]] Meanwhile, the takeover of Bintulu Port by the Sarawak Government followed negotiations between the two governments before the deal was finalised in June. The Sarawak Government officially took over the management and administration of Bintulu Port on Sept 1, following the repeal of the Bintulu Port Authority Act, which came into effect on Aug 31.

items.title: Senior citizen suffers burns after motorcycle catches fire in Jelutong
items.summary: The Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 2.05pm involving a Honda EX5 at Jalan Lenggong, Symphony Park. Firefighters from the Jalan Perak fire and rescue station brought the blaze under control at 2.15pm. Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the motorcycle was estimated to have been 60 per cent damaged in the fire.

items.title: [UPDATED] 'Please have mercy': Tasek Bera Orang Asli seek talks over eviction
items.summary: BERA: Orang Asli villagers living near Tasek Bera are seeking negotiations with the authorities after receiving notices in June ordering them to vacate parts of the forest reserve, saying the land has been their source of livelihood for generations. Kampung Pathir Tok Batin Amir Noor Tan, 49, said several Orang Asli villages around Tasek Bera received pink warning notices from the Forestry Department in June for allegedly encroaching into the permanent forest reserve. he said.

items.title: Haze: Selangor to review follow-up measures on Friday
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Selangor government will review follow-up measures to address the deteriorating haze situation, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. He said the matter would be discussed in detail, based on reports from all relevant parties, at the Selangor state executive council meeting scheduled for Friday. Six areas in Selangor recorded Air Pollution Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4.30pm today.

items.title: PM Anwar: Malaysia supports and appreciates Saudi Arabia’s efforts following drone interception in Mecca
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Malaysia has expressed its support for Saudi Arabia following the successful interception of a drone near Mecca, asserting that any attempt to threaten the security and sanctity of Islam’s holiest city is completely unacceptable. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia appreciates the swift action taken to safeguard the safety of residents and pilgrims in Mecca. “I have been following reports on a drone that was successfully intercepted near Makkah al-Mukarramah.

items.title: DOE records 1,418 enforcement, monitoring actions amid haze
items.summary: Its deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said the actions included 978 monitoring activities, 83 field directives, 31 instruction notices, 305 cases referred to other agencies for further action, 11 compound offers, and 10 land title searches to support investigations and court proceedings. "These efforts reflect the DOE's ongoing commitment to detecting and preventing open burning, as well as taking action against potential sources of pollution that could worsen air quality during haze episodes," she said in a statement today. She said enforcement efforts are also strengthened through inspections and patrols in areas identified as high-risk, including agricultural land, peatlands, plantations, landfill sites and locations prone to open burning.

items.title: MCA ready for GE16 if polls called early, says Wee
items.summary: BATU PAHAT: MCA is ready to face the 16th General Election (GE16) earlier than scheduled, party president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said. "MCA must ensure that election machinery and strategies are put in place early, including taking into account the different political conditions in each state," he said. He said MCA's approach could not be standardised across all states, as Johor, Negri Sembilan and Melaka each had different political characteristics and varying levels of party strength.

items.title: KL attractions see many visitors going maskless amid haze on Malaysia Day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Many people are still choosing not to wear face masks despite the haze, particularly at popular public attractions. A check at the Sultan Abdul Samad Building and KLCC found many visitors going about their activities without masks. Visitor Norherma Mokhtar, 35, said she opted not to wear one as she found it uncomfortable.

items.title: PH has yet to discuss Melaka polls with Rauf, says Amirudin
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: No discussions have been held with Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh on cooperation for the upcoming Melaka election, said Pakatan Harapan election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. Amirudin, who is also PKR vice-president and Selangor Menteri Besar, said he had yet to discuss the state election with Rauf. He said the decision on when to dissolve the Melaka Legislative Assembly was up to the chief minister.

items.title: Palestinians are the real victims, Thunberg tells Ed Sheeran
items.summary: STOCKHOLM: Swedish activist Greta Thunberg and other activists have called out British superstar Ed Sheeran after rapper Macklemore was dropped from his tour for making pro-Palestinian comments while performing. Sheeran has denied being behind the decision to remove Macklemore, saying his tour's promoter was responsible, but several supporting acts have announced they were quitting the tour. "Ed, there is only one victim here: the Palestinian people," Thunberg, together with activist group Humanti Project, said in post to Instagram late on Tuesday.

items.title: Fuel prices rise 35 sen amid Middle East tensions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The retail prices of RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and unsubsidised diesel will rise by 35 sen a litre for the Sept 17 to 23 period, according to the Finance Ministry. It said unsubsidised diesel will rise from RM4.92 to RM5.27 a litre. Eligible Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel) recipients will continue to pay RM2.10 a litre for diesel, compared with the unsubsidised price of RM5.27.

items.title: Selangor MB: Follow-up haze measures to be reviewed on Friday
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 — The Selangor government will review follow-up measures to address the deteriorating haze situation, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. He said the matter would be discussed in detail, based on reports from all relevant parties, at the Selangor State Executive Council meeting scheduled for Friday. Six areas in Selangor recorded Air Pollution Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4.30 pm today.

items.title: Keretapi Sarong: Media Prima truck draws visitors at TRX
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Media Prima Berhad's (MPB) "Wajah Malaysia" mobile truck drew visitors at the 2026 Keretapi Sarong event at The Exchange TRX here today with free personalised newspaper front-page prints and interactive activities. MPB Group Marketing manager Hana Hatim said visitors to the Petronas-sponsored truck could have their photographs taken and receive a free personalised A3-sized newspaper front page. Visitor Nur Irsya Humaira, 20, a student, said today was her first time attending Keretapi Sarong and described the experience as lively and meaningful.

items.title: Former Kosovo president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
items.summary: THE HAGUE: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci was found guilty of war crimes including murder, torture and illegal detention by the Kosovo war crimes tribunal on Wednesday. Thaci, 58, was sentenced to 25 years in prison for crimes committed as top commander of the ethnic Albanian Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) during the territory's violent break from Serbia in the 1990s. Thaci remains a revered figure for many Kosovo Albanians, while the tribunal itself is deeply unpopular in Kosovo.

items.title: Haze alert: 38 areas in Peninsular Malaysia record unhealthy readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A total of 38 areas in Peninsular Malaysia recorded unhealthy Air Pollution Index (API) readings as of 5 pm today. According to the API management system (APIMS) portal, six areas in Selangor - Johan Setia (183), Shah Alam (170), Petaling Jaya (164), Klang (160) as well as Banting and Kuala Selangor (159), two areas in Kuala Lumpur - Cheras (174) and Batu Muda (170), three areas in Negeri Sembilan - Nilai (170), Seremban (165) and Port Dickson (148), along with Putrajaya (170) - recorded API readings at the unhealthy level. Down south in Johor, three areas recorded unhealthy API readings - Tangkak (134), Kluang (124) and Batu Pahat (103), as well as three areas in Melaka - Bukit Rambai (155), Alor Gajah (153) and Bandaraya Melaka (145).

items.title: MMNOs face DNB accounting test in Q4
items.summary: CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd each hold a 33.3 per cent stake in DNB - and its equity accounting treatment is expected to materialise in Q4. "Under our bear and bull scenarios, CelcomDigi offers 37 per cent upside and 26 per cent downside, compared with 21 per cent upside and 20 per cent downside for Maxis," it said. Kenanga Research said Maxis has less valuation cushion, as it already trades at historical mean.

items.title: Indonesia seals off 50 companies over forest and land fires
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia has sealed off 50 companies across eight provinces after forest and land fire hotspots were identified within their operational areas. Social media updates from the ministry showed that among the six priority provinces, Central Kalimantan recorded 266 hotspots, South Sumatra 245, South Kalimantan 72, Jambi 62, West Kalimantan 43, and Riau 15. Hotspot numbers declined in Central, West, and South Kalimantan, while increases were recorded in South Sumatra, Jambi, and Riau, requiring continued intensive monitoring.

items.title: Anwar says Tabung Haji asked to delay RCI report release
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) had asked the government to delay the release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report after it was completed, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar said TH management made the request out of concern that releasing the report would trigger a mass withdrawal of deposits, potentially affecting its operations. He said the matter was subsequently brought before the cabinet before a decision was made to delay the release of the report.

items.title: New-generation MyKad applications open tomorrow with enhanced security features
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — The National Registration Department (NRD) has unveiled the new-generation MyKad with a redesigned appearance and enhanced security features. The new card incorporates several security elements on both its front and back, including a Dynamic Security Hologram and transparent window on the front. He said the new MyKad has about 50 additional security features, which will be introduced in phases.

items.title: Malaysia Day: PM Anwar calls for renewed commitment to unity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Malaysia Day serves as a reminder that the nation was built on a covenant between the government and the people, between the regions and the Federation, and between loyalty and justice, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Happy Malaysia Day!" he said.

items.title: Woman killed, sister and motorcyclist seriously injured after lorry hits their stalled car in Nilai
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A woman was killed while her sister and a motorcyclist were seriously injured after a lorry crashed into their broken-down car at Kilometre 284.4 of the North-South Expressway northbound near Nilai this morning. Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said the district traffic complaints counter received information about the accident from the Nilai district police operations room at 9.01am. Johari said a 22-year-old man riding a Honda RS 150 arrived at the scene and tried to help the woman move the vehicle.

items.title: Malaysia to seek preventive measures, diplomatic cooperation over transboundary haze, says Zahid
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 16 — Malaysia prioritises long-term diplomatic cooperation and early preventive measures over seeking compensation from neighbouring countries in addressing the issue of transboundary haze, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Ahmad Zahid, who is also National Disaster Management Committee Chairman, said a prudent and structured diplomatic approach is the most effective way to address sensitive issues among Asean member states while ensuring optimal technical coordination. Also present were Sarawak Deputy Premier and Chairman of the Sarawak State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN), Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas, and Deputy Minister of Rural and Regional Development, Datuk Rubiah Wang.

items.title: Anwar to review impact of electricity bill increase at special meeting tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A special meeting will be held tomorrow with the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA), the Energy Commission (EC), Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) and the Ministry of Finance (MoF). The meeting will review immediate mitigation measures to reduce the impact of the electricity bill increase on affected households. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that upon his return from India and the Maldives, his attention remained focused on the people’s concerns regarding the recent increase in electricity bills.

items.title: Policeman injured while chasing 4WD involved in Kluang cable theft case
items.summary: Kluang deputy police chief Superintendent Nik Mohd Azmi Husin said the incident is believed to have occurred at 5.54am when two policemen on motorcycles were chasing a Mitsubishi vehicle. He said the suspect, believed to be involved in an earlier cable theft incident, had an uncut cable at the rear of the vehicle. Nik Mohd Azmi was responding to a video posted on Threads showing two policemen chasing a red Mitsubishi pick-up truck in Kluang town.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan DOE ramps up enforcement as haze hits unhealthy levels
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 16 — The Negeri Sembilan Department of Environment (DOE) is stepping up ground-level monitoring, particularly on open burning activities, following worsening haze conditions in several districts in the state. State DOE director Abdul Aziz Parmin said other sources being closely monitored included factories, quarries, motor vehicles, development projects, land clearing and any activities that could contribute to dust emissions and cause air pollution. He said all actions related to the haze situation would be referred to the National Haze Action Plan, while at the state level, the department would continuously update the State Disaster Management Committee on the situation.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh: My views on Najib’s pardon given honestly
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 —Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said she had expressed her views on former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s pardon application during the Pardons Board meeting on Sept 11, after reviewing the written opinion of the Attorney General. The statement was issued in response to remarks by Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said regarding the deferment of Najib’s pardon application. Hannah said she had expressed her views in her capacity as the minister responsible for the Federal Territories.

items.title: Schools advised to stagger students seeking medical checks, says Perak health exco
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 16 — The Perak government has advised schools to coordinate with District Health Offices and relevant health facilities before bringing large numbers of students for medical examinations following an outbreak. The advice came after a boarding school in Ipoh brought 57 students with Influenza-Like Illness (ILI) to a nearby health clinic simultaneously, despite being advised to bring them in stages. Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said bringing symptomatic students in stages would help prevent congestion at health facilities and reduce the risk of infection transmission.

items.title: Guan Eng: Umno no longer brings value to Penang government amid cooperation with Perikatan, PAS
items.summary: Lim said Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Chow Kon Yeow appeared more focused on criticising him than addressing Umno’s recent attacks on PH, creating what he described as an impression that Chow feared Umno might quit the state government. “Instead of hitting back at Umno for working with the opposition PN, Chow chose to criticise me,” Lim said, adding that Penang PH leaders should not be afraid of offending “an extremist Umno” that he claimed had indulged in divisive rhetoric against non-Muslim minorities and shown little inclusivity toward non-Malays. Even without Umno’s two assemblymen, Lim said, PH would still command a two‑thirds majority in the Penang legislative assembly.

items.title: Perak exco: 46 students at Influenza A cluster school suffer flu-like illness
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 16 — Forty-six students at a boarding school in Ipoh have been diagnosed with influenza-like illness (ILI) following an Influenza A cluster detected at the school, Perak Human Resources, Health, Indian Community Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman A. Sivanesan said. He said the cases were identified after health officials screened and assessed 61 students with symptoms up to Sept 14, while 14 others were found to have upper respiratory tract infections and one had conjunctivitis. According to him, the school had first brought 57 symptomatic students to a nearby health clinic on Monday, before the figure rose to 61 when an additional 39 symptomatic students were brought in yesterday.

items.title: Raja Muda of Selangor, MACC chief commissioner discuss anti-corruption initiatives
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 — Efforts to strengthen the fight against corruption were among the matters discussed by Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman. The MACC said the matter was discussed when Tengku Amir Shah granted an audience to Abd Halim at Istana Selangor, Bukit Kiara, last Monday. In a statement today, the commission said Tengku Amir Shah was also briefed on its latest developments and ongoing initiatives, particularly those relating to anti-corruption efforts in Selangor.

items.title: Sanusi: Too early for seat talks as Kedah PAS, Umno explore political cooperation
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Sept 16 — Kedah PAS and Umno are focusing on creating a positive environment for further discussions on political cooperation, with no requests yet made over seat allocations, Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor reportedly said. The Umno delegation was led by Kedah Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Mahdzir Khalid and Alor Setar Umno division chief and former Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Ahmad Bashah Md Hanipah. PAS was represented by Kedah commissioner and PAS Central Ulama Council chief Datuk Ahmad Yahya, deputy commissioner II Dr Ahmad Fakhruddin Sheikh Fakhrurazi and Kedah secretary Senator Musoddaq Ahmad.

items.title: Penang air quality hits unhealthy levels statewide, Minden records API of 167
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 16 — Air quality at all four monitoring stations in Penang reached unhealthy levels as of 11am today, with Minden recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 167. State Housing and Environment Committee chairman Datuk Seri S. Sundarajoo said Balik Pulau recorded an API reading of 164, followed by Seberang Jaya at 162 and Seberang Perai at 160. He said Minden and Balik Pulau had registered unhealthy readings over the past 24 hours, while readings in Seberang Jaya and Seberang Perai had risen from moderate to unhealthy levels.

items.title: Police: Sri Petaling bomb scare turns out to be team-building game equipment left behind by worker
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A suspicious plastic box found unattended in front of a shoplot in Bandar Baru Sri Petaling earlier today contained toy building blocks belonging to a company that organises training and team-building programmes, police said today. Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said police were contacted by a company director, who informed them that the unattended plastic box belonged to his company. “Investigations found that the box had been left behind by a company employee and contained 20 plastic toy blocks from a game called ‘Radioactive Bomb’, which are used as equipment for group team-building activities.

items.title: MA63 still binding, no ‘new deal’ needed, says Armizan
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 16 — The Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) did not cease to exist upon the enactment of the Federal Constitution but remains in force, with the commitments and responsibilities contained therein continuing to be relevant and binding on all parties, said Minister of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. “This term reaffirms the commitment and responsibility of all parties that agreed to sign the agreement to form the Federation of Malaysia,” he said in a Facebook post in conjunction with Malaysia Day today. Armizan said Malaysia, which was formed in 1963, has now reached 63 years, although Sept 16 only became an important date in the official national calendar and was officially celebrated as Malaysia Day from 2010.

items.title: KLIA standardises e-hailing entry fees at RM2 across both terminals effective today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) has standardised the entry fee for e-hailing vehicles at RM2, inclusive of tax, across Terminal 1 and Terminal 2, effective today. Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) in a statement here said the revised fee also represents a reduction from the previous charges of RM3 at Terminal 1 and RM2.16 at Terminal 2, providing passengers with a single, consistent rate for e-hailing pick-ups at both terminals. Meanwhile, Senior General Manager for Passenger Experience at KLIA Abd Hasman Abd Muhimin said the continued enhancements to KLIA’s e-hailing facilities reflect the airport operator’s commitment to improving the overall passenger journey while ensuring that airport operations remain orderly, efficient and responsive to evolving needs.

items.title: Fahmi says Sarawak redelineation has begun but gives no election deadline (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 16 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil made no commitment on whether the electoral boundary review would be completed before the next Sarawak election, but stressed that the process had already begun. Fahmi highlighted the commitment by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the EC to expedite the redelineation process. Meanwhile, EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said in a statement on Sept 13 that the commission would carry out the review of electoral boundaries subject to amendments to the Federal Constitution.

items.title: Home Ministry vows to crush foreign worker fraud syndicates ‘at the root’
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 16 — The Home Ministry (KDN) is determined to dismantle the operations of syndicates manipulating the foreign worker system and falsifying documents at the root, without any tolerance, said its Minister, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the Immigration Department (JIM) was no longer taking a defensive approach, but was instead acting aggressively to cripple the syndicates at their source. Saifuddin Nasution said the fake e-PLKS were sold for RM150 each, while the fake police reports were sold for RM70 each.

items.title: Haze flips west: 41 areas in Peninsular Malaysia hit unhealthy levels as Sabah, Sarawak clear
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — A total of 41 areas in Peninsular Malaysia recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 9 am today. According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, six areas in Selangor recorded unhealthy readings, namely Johan Setia (187), Shah Alam (175), Petaling Jaya (169), Klang (167), Banting (166) and Kuala Selangor (164). In Penang, four areas recorded unhealthy readings, namely Minden (166), Balik Pulau (164), Seberang Jaya (162) and Seberang Perai (160).

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of heavy rain and strong winds across Penang, Sabah and Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds affecting several areas in Sarawak and Sabah until 11am today, as well as the whole of Penang until noon. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the affected areas in Sarawak are Limbang, Miri (Miri and Subis), and Kuching (Lundu and Kuching). In Sabah, the warning covers the West Coast areas of Penampang, Putatan, Papar, Tuaran, Ranau and Kota Kinabalu, as well as the Interior areas of Membakut, Beaufort, Kuala Penyu, Tambunan, Keningau and Tenom.

items.title: Malaysia Day: Selangor Sultan urges Malaysians to strengthen unity, cherish peace
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 16 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has called on Malaysians to continue strengthening unity and appreciate the peace and harmony enjoyed by the country in conjunction with the Malaysia Day celebration today. “Happy Malaysia Day, Malaysia!” said His Royal Highness.

items.title: Nearly nine in 10 intimate-partner murders in Malaysia since 2017 were unplanned, police say
items.summary: Of the intimate-partner cases, 99 involved married couples, eight involved former husbands killing their former wives and 58 involved boyfriends and girlfriends. Among the 21 killings where police found evidence of prior planning, six involved husbands killing their wives, two involved wives killing their husbands and four involved former husbands killing their former wives. Of the 144 cases without prior planning, 76 involved husbands killing their wives, 15 involved wives killing their husbands, four involved former husbands killing their former wives, 42 involved boyfriends killing their girlfriends and seven involved girlfriends killing their boyfriends.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh wants KL to compete with Singapore as regional concert hub
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Kuala Lumpur should compete with Singapore for major international concerts rather than have Malaysian fans cross the border to watch their favourite acts, Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh said, according to The Straits Times (ST). Why should my people in Kuala Lumpur go to Singapore to watch concerts and not here? The comments come as Malaysia seeks to position Kuala Lumpur as a bigger player in Southeast Asia’s live entertainment market, with the government lowering regulatory and cost barriers for international acts.

items.title: Malaysia loses US$775m a year to illicit tobacco trade as market share hits 55pc, study finds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 16 — Malaysia is estimated to be losing around US$775 million (RM3.2 billion) in tax revenue annually to illicit tobacco, with illegal products accounting for more than half of the market, according to a new regional study. According to CME, the estimated revenue lost to illicit tobacco in both Malaysia and Pakistan now exceeds the amount governments collect from tobacco taxation, suggesting significant erosion of the legal tax base. That translates to nearly US$48 in estimated revenue lost for every US$100 collected in tobacco taxes.
